newsitem.title: BRAZIL: MOTOR RACING-WILLIAMS DUO DETERMINED TO BOUNCE BACK IN BRAZIL.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-WILLIAMS DUO DETERMINED TO BOUNCE BACK IN BRAZIL.

text.p: Three weeks after their unexpected exit from the season-opening Australian Grand Prix, Williams duo Jacques Villeneuve and Heinz-Harald Frentzen are determined to bounce back in triumph in this weekend's Brazilian Grand Prix.

Canadian Villeneuve, the pre-season favourite to succeed Briton Damon Hill as world drivers' champion, crashed out in Australia at the first corner after starting from pole position while German Frentzen drove strongly among the leaders before spinning off with a brake problem.

The joint exits made it easy for Briton David Coulthard to give McLaren their first victory in 50 outings since the last triumph of the late Ayrton Senna at Adelaide in 1993. But, this time, the pair are intent on making it quite a different story.

"It was both annoying and frustrating to throw away all the good work in Australia but I think we showed in qualifying that we have a really great car," said Villeneuve. "The speed is there for all to see and all we have to do in Brazil is stay out of trouble and demonstrate it in the race."

Since the first-corner fracas in Melbourne -- triggered by an unrepentant Eddie Irvine who forced his Ferrari down the inside of Villeneuve and Briton Johnny Herbert's Sauber, taking all three of them off the track -- Villeneuve and Frentzen have been testing at the Le Castellet track in France.

Much of their work focused on curing the braking problem which bedevilled them in Australia and, according to the team, they have succeeded. Villeneuve, who spun off last year in Brazil in torrential rain, is expecting to go the distance and to win.
But he is likely to face a strong challenge from Frentzen who is hungry to prove he has the ability to race and finish at the front.
"Things didn't work out in Australia but I am confident about Brazil," he said. "We were disappointed, but we have worked hard to rectify the problems and now I think we are ready."
The biggest challenge to the Williams may come from Benetton who have also worked hard to improve their all-round performance after a disappointing opening race.
Major aerodynamic revisions are expected around the air-intake area of the car, an improvement which could propel Austrian Gerhard Berger and his French team mate Jean Alesi into good positions.

Ferrari, led by double champion Michael Schumacher and Irvine, have continued to struggle to extract the best from their cars and could be edged out by McLaren, buoyant after their surprise victory and third place in Melbourne.

"The whole team is buzzing," said Coulthard, 25, who has sprayed his hair silver as part of a bet he took for winning. "It has brought the whole factory alive and everyone is feeling good about the next few races." He and team mate Mika Hakkinen of Finland are likely to be threats to the Williams men.

Last year's winner and champion Hill, however, is not expected to make much impact. He failed to start in Australia, after a throttle problem on the formation lap, and has tested ferociously to improve the reliability of his Arrows car. "We are hoping for better things but that is all you can say," he admitted.

At least Hill, and Arrows, will be taking part. The new Lola team, which failed to qualify with either car in Australia, is now out of the championship series after withdrawing due to financial and technical problems.

This will reduce the entries for Sunday's 71-lap race on the Interlagos track to 22 for what promises to be a demanding test of reliability and character for cars and drivers in the humid and hot conditions.
